assist.label: Set up with your agent
assist.prompt:
Help me set up the Slack (as you) connector using the Browser plugin. I want to stay in control of every sign-in and approval.

Rules:
- Never ask for, read, type or reveal a password, a 2FA code or the app's Client Secret. If Slack needs me to sign in, open the sign-in page in the Browser view and wait for me to finish.
- Say what you are about to do before each step, and take a screenshot after it so I can follow along. Use browser_view so I can watch.
- If a page does not match what I describe, observe it and adapt. If you are unsure, ask me. If Slack blocks a step (admin approval, a workspace policy), stop and tell me exactly what it says. Do not retry or work around it.

Steps:
1. Call browser_profiles. If a saved profile is already signed in to Slack, ask me whether to use it. Otherwise open a new profile at https://slack.com/signin, ask me to sign in to the workspace I want, and wait.
2. Open this link. It opens Slack's Create an app dialog with Dimension's app manifest already filled in (user permissions to read and send as me, MCP on, PKCE on, redirect http://localhost:53682/callback):
https://api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json=%7B%22display_information%22%3A%7B%22name%22%3A%22Dimension%20(as%20you)%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22Lets%20your%20Dimension%20agent%20read%20and%20send%20Slack%20messages%20as%20you%2C%20through%20Slack's%20MCP%20server.%22%7D%2C%22oauth_config%22%3A%7B%22redirect_urls%22%3A%5B%22http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A53682%2Fcallback%22%5D%2C%22scopes%22%3A%7B%22user%22%3A%5B%22canvases%3Aread%22%2C%22canvases%3Awrite%22%2C%22channels%3Ahistory%22%2C%22channels%3Aread%22%2C%22channels%3Awrite%22%2C%22chat%3Awrite%22%2C%22emoji%3Aread%22%2C%22files%3Aread%22%2C%22files%3Awrite%22%2C%22groups%3Ahistory%22%2C%22groups%3Aread%22%2C%22groups%3Awrite%22%2C%22im%3Ahistory%22%2C%22im%3Aread%22%2C%22im%3Awrite%22%2C%22lists%3Aread%22%2C%22lists%3Awrite%22%2C%22mpim%3Ahistory%22%2C%22mpim%3Aread%22%2C%22mpim%3Awrite%22%2C%22reactions%3Aread%22%2C%22reactions%3Awrite%22%2C%22search%3Aread.files%22%2C%22search%3Aread.im%22%2C%22search%3Aread.mpim%22%2C%22search%3Aread.private%22%2C%22search%3Aread.public%22%2C%22search%3Aread.users%22%2C%22users%3Aread%22%2C%22users%3Aread.email%22%5D%7D%2C%22pkce_enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%22settings%22%3A%7B%22org_deploy_enabled%22%3Afalse%2C%22socket_mode_enabled%22%3Afalse%2C%22token_rotation_enabled%22%3Atrue%2C%22is_mcp_enabled%22%3Atrue%7D%7D
3. Choose the workspace I name (ask me if there is more than one), click Next, check that the summary shows the user scopes and no errors, then click Create.
4. On the new app's Basic Information page, find App Credentials and read ONLY the Client ID (it looks like 1234567890.1234567890123). Do not open or copy the Client Secret.
5. Give me the Client ID and tell me what to do next: open Plugins, choose Slack (as you), click Connect, paste the Client ID, pick Read and send, and click Allow when Slack asks. If Slack says an admin must approve the app, tell me who to ask.
6. Close the browser tab you opened.

setup.title: Create the Slack app (one click)
setup.detail: This opens Slack's Create an app screen with everything filled in: the permissions to read and send as you, MCP switched on, PKCE on, and the localhost sign-in address. Pick your workspace, click Next, then Create.

setup.title: Get it approved, if Slack asks
setup.detail: Some workspaces make you ask an admin before an app can sign anyone in. If Slack says so, send them the app's page and wait. Dimension cannot get around that.

setup.title: Copy the Client ID
setup.detail: On the app's Basic Information page, under App Credentials, copy the Client ID. It is not a secret, and you do not need the Client Secret.

setup.title: Paste it below, choose what Dimension may do, and click Connect
setup.detail: Slack opens in your browser: click Allow. Port 53682 must be free while you connect. If Slack (as you) goes unused for about 30 days Slack can sign it out; click Connect again.

form.label: Client ID
form.help: From your Slack app's Basic Information page, under App Credentials. It is not a secret.

form.label: Client Secret (leave blank)
form.help: Leave this blank. The app uses PKCE, which needs no secret. Fill it in only if Slack rejects the connection with bad_client_secret.

scopeOptions.label: Read only
scopeOptions.detail: Search and read channels, threads, DMs, files, canvases and lists. Nothing can be sent.

scopeOptions.label: Read and send
scopeOptions.detail: Everything above, plus sending and scheduling messages and adding reactions, as you. Every send asks you first.

scopeOptions.label: Everything
scopeOptions.detail: Adds creating channels, writing canvases and lists, and uploading files.

failures.title: Reconnect Slack (as you)
failures.detail: Slack no longer accepts the saved sign-in. Click Connect again and allow access.

failures.title: Your workspace has not approved this app
failures.detail: Ask a workspace admin to approve the Dimension app, then click Connect again.

tools.name: slack_tools
tools.description: List what Slack's official MCP server can do for you, or describe one tool in full. Each tool is marked read or write.

tools.name: slack_read
tools.description: Run one read-only Slack tool as you: search, read a channel or thread, find users and channels, read a canvas.

tools.name: slack_act
tools.description: Run one Slack tool that changes Slack as you: send, schedule, react, create. DESTRUCTIVE: you are asked to approve every call.
